body: Warlocked is Bits Studios' Game Boy Color real-time strategy game, placing human and beast armies in separate campaigns. Workers gather resources, structures support development and military units confront the opposing force while the action continues. The overhead battlefield fits the familiar organisation of a larger computer strategy game into the handheld's limited display and controls. The player still has several responsibilities at once: reveal the surrounding terrain, maintain the settlement and send an appropriate group toward the place where the next threat is developing.

Archers, other soldiers and specialised wizards give the two factions different responses to an enemy formation. Magical abilities can weaken opponents or transform them, making a discovered wizard valuable for more than another unit in the crowd. Fog of war hides unexplored ground, requiring an army to move before the whole situation becomes visible. Decisions about exploration and combat therefore affect each other. A route may reveal a useful opportunity, but reaching it safely depends on the force assembled before leaving the protection of the base.

Two players can compete using linked Game Boy Color systems, and wizards can also be traded between copies. Those features give the collected spellcasters a role beyond one campaign. Jeroen Tel composed the music for the British-developed game, which Nintendo published in North America in 2000. Warlocked's unusual achievement is preserving the relationship between economy, exploration and a moving army on a compact portable machine. The simplified presentation still leaves the player making recognisable strategic choices about where resources should go and what the next group of units needs to accomplish.
story_headings: Command a small army on a very small screen
A wizard changes what the army can do
A strategy game built for the link cable
